app_rules.float.help:
Floating takes this app's matching windows out of tiling: each keeps its last position and size and appears on every space, instead of living in one space's grid.

This is per-app floating — not the **Floating** layout mode, which floats every window in a space.
app_rules.override.caption: Space assignments made here apply to this profile only. Dimmed rows are inherited from the app-wide base rules and stay in sync with them; picking another space overrides the rule for this profile, and deleting a row un-pins the app here even when the base pins it. To edit the base rules themselves — or the Float column, which is always app-wide — switch back to the currently loaded profile in the header's picker.

layout.schematic.bsp.ax: BSP preview: width ratio %1$d percent, height ratio %2$d percent; the plus tile is where the next window lands.
layout.schematic.bsp.caption_alternating: Splits alternate horizontal then vertical; the + tile is where the next window opens.
layout.schematic.bsp.caption_longest: Each split cuts the longer side; the + tile is where the next window opens.
layout.schematic.grid.caption_rigid: A fixed %1$d × %2$d grid; each window shrinks to a cell, extras stack in the last.
layout.schematic.grid.caption_rigid_auto: A fixed grid sized to your screen (about 3 × 3); each window shrinks to a cell.
layout.schematic.grid.order_columns: New windows fill across a row, then wrap down.
layout.schematic.grid.order_rows: New windows fill down a column, then wrap across.
layout.schematic.monocle.ax: Monocle preview: one window fills the screen; focus cycles through the others.
layout.schematic.monocle.caption_h: All windows fill the screen; new ones come to the front, and focus cycles left/right.
layout.schematic.monocle.caption_v: All windows fill the screen; new ones come to the front, and focus cycles up/down.
layout.schematic.scrolling.ax: Scrolling preview: a row of windows framed by the screen, continuing off both edges; the anchor window holds focus.
layout.schematic.scrolling.caption: Focus rests at the anchor; the row scrolls off past it. The + is where the next window opens.
layout.schematic.scrolling.follow_ax: Follow preview: two frames — the focus steps one slot over and the viewport pans just enough to reveal it, leaving the previous window visible.
layout.schematic.scrolling.follow_b: When focus steps to the next window
layout.schematic.scrolling.follow_captio: The viewport holds still and pans the minimum to reveal the focus, keeping the side you came from in view.
layout.schematic.stack.ax: Stack preview: %1$d master windows, master ratio %2$d percent; the plus tile is where the next window lands.
layout.schematic.stack.caption_all: Master column beside the stack; when the stack fills, the whole column piles so only the top edges show.
layout.schematic.stack.caption_overflow: Master column beside the stack; when the stack fills, the surplus piles at the bottom.
layout.schematic.track.ax: Track preview: tracks along one axis, the far one piling overflow; the plus is the next window.
layout.schematic.track.caption_focused: New windows join the focused track; the far track piles the overflow.
layout.schematic.track.caption_own: New windows open their own track; the far track piles the overflow.

layout_defaults.min_window_size_caption: Windows never tile smaller than this. It also sets the auto-size grid's cell size.
layout_params.overflow.stack.help:
**Cascade overflow** — Keeps as many windows fully tiled as fit, then cascades only the extra ones at the bottom.
**Cascade all** — Cascades the whole stack, showing a sliver of every window.
layout_params.overflow.track.help:
How the far-edge **overflow track** — which collects the tracks that don't fit side by side — packs its windows.
**Cascade all** (the default) — piles every window from the top.
**Cascade overflow** — tiles what fits, piles the rest.
An ordinary track that holds more windows than fit always overflows this second way; only the far-edge track is configurable.
layout_params.split_ratio_h.help: How much of a side-by-side split's width goes to the earlier window; the later window gets the rest. Applies to every left/right split.
layout_params.split_ratio_v.help: How much of a stacked split's height goes to the earlier window; the later window gets the rest. Applies to every top/bottom split.
layout_params.split_strategy.help:
**Longest side** — Cuts whichever side of the region is longer, keeping new windows close to square.
**Alternating** — Alternates left/right and top/bottom cuts as the layout gets deeper, regardless of shape.
layout_params.wrap_focus.help: When on, moving focus past the last window wraps around to the first, and past the first back to the last, instead of stopping at the end.
lua_editor.adopt.title: Adopt this config into the visual editor?
lua_editor.adopt_help.body: Nothing is lost: your current code isn't deleted, it's kept as a commented-out backup in init.lua. Gaps, layouts, rules, and keybindings are imported; a shortcut that can't be read back stays in the backup — re-add it in the Shortcuts section.

2. Find KiwiDesk in the list and turn it on.
3. Come back here — we detect it automatically.

onboarding.spaces.body:
KiwiDesk maps virtual spaces to specific monitors. For that, macOS needs “Displays have separate Spaces” turned on.

Enable it in System Settings › Desktop & Dock, then log out and back in. You can also skip this and set it up later.
onboarding.spaces.title: Displays have separate Spaces
onboarding.welcome.body:
KiwiDesk arranges your windows automatically. To move and resize windows of other apps, macOS requires you to grant Accessibility permission.

KiwiDesk never reads your keystrokes and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection.

shortcuts.modes.caption: Modes are alternate shortcut sets — only the active mode's shortcuts fire. Bind a key below to switch between them. “default” is the standard mode and is always the active one after the app starts.

shortcuts.size_float.layouts_caption: Grow/Shrink only applies in the bsp, stack, scrolling, and track layouts; it is a no-op in monocle, grid, and floating.
